newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Islamic rebels free last hostages in Tajikistan.
newsitem.headline: Islamic rebels free last hostages in Tajikistan.

text.p: An Islamic rebel group in Tajikistan on Monday freed the last five hostages it held, a Tajik government official told Reuters.

The official said Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov, who had negotiated the release of the five, all U.N workers, greeted them at the village of Obigarm, some 80 km (50 miles) to the east of the capital Dushanbe.
The official said that all five freed hostages -- two U.N. military observers and three workers with the U.N. refugee agency -- were on the way to Dushanbe.

The crisis erupted on February 4 when a rebel group led by Bakhrom Sadirov seized the first of the hostages and demanded that the government allow Bakhrom's brother Rizvon and some 40 supporters to join him from neighbouring Afghanistan.

The Tajik authorities allowed more than 30 armed fighters to reach Sadirov's base on Saturday on the understanding that he would then free all his captives. Initially there were 15 hostages. But only 10 of them were released, in phases.
Rakhmonov, clearly under heavy pressure from Moscow to settle the crisis, flew to Obigarm on Monday morning to negotiate directly with the hostage takers.
